newsitem.title: USA: Vermont court to hear part of school funding suit.
newsitem.headline: Vermont court to hear part of school funding suit.

text.p: Vermont Supreme Court has agreed to hear legal arguments on a lawsuit challenging the funding of public schools with local property taxes.
A trial on the issue was expected to start today in Vermont Superior Court in Hyde Park, but that now must wait until the high court settles some issues.

Both the state and the American Civil Liberties Union, which wants schools funded equally with statewide taxes, appealed Judge John Meeker's pre-trial ruling that rejected what they considered key parts of the suit.

The ACLU has claimed that the Vermont and federal constitutions require schools to provide an equal education for pupils in every locality. Funding the schools with property taxes, which can vary widely, means that the amount spent per student in different districts differs, and it wants the state to equalize funding.
